### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, touching **140** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 06060c61c572f833f19497a6e84838c52a923166`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 06060c61c572f833f19497a6e84838c52a923166` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2bd010e8db3def7961ff5bb55f14a00e29061414` — the merge of head `ee1c0183fa49234f4617984d219614a811b05878` into base `06060c61c572f833f19497a6e84838c52a923166`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2bd010e8db3def7961ff5bb55f14a00e29061414 && git checkout 2bd010e8db3def7961ff5bb55f14a00e29061414
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 06060c61c572f833f19497a6e84838c52a923166 ee1c0183fa49234f4617984d219614a811b05878 && git checkout -B drift-repro 06060c61c572f833f19497a6e84838c52a923166 && git merge --no-ff ee1c0183fa49234f4617984d219614a811b05878

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 06060c61c572f833f19497a6e84838c52a923166
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 06060c61c572f833f19497a6e84838c52a923166` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a535d01808057b7c921d5b50a4b0567aa7ad391a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-oracle-dialect.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-field-mapping.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-sqlite-serialisation.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-crud.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-sequence-semantics.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-bulk-operations.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-aggregation.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-distinct.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-window-functions.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-query-plan.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-schema-sync.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-oracle-dialect.test.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-oracle-federation-conformance.test.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-compile-refusal-seam.test.ts + packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-top-level.ts (`withheldFilterError`, the `VALIDATION_ERROR` write-refusal family), packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-oracle-introspection.ts (`rowsOf`, the measured `knex.raw` row shape on `oracledb`), packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-internal-helpers.ts (`readableIdsSubquery`), packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-predicate-emitters.ts (`applyNormalizedComparison`), packages/spec/src/data/type-compat.ts on `main` (the `oracle` / `uuid` `demoteExact` rule the narrowing is judged against)

Face: `reviewFace` returns no `hits` on this file list (no published schema, no governed path); the PR declares `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, and the dev's own open question says some inputs that reached Oracle on `main` are now refused before they are sent. Reviewed on the narrowing face at the seat's request: every non-prose path of the diff is in scope, the cited code is read, never reviewed. The `.changeset` file is prose and is judged in ② only. Inputs: card #31390 (body and all four comments, the os-dev-report 6725220789 included), PR #31642 (body, file list, net diff against `main`), and the check-runs on the head. The tree was judged, not the PR body's account of it.

Check-runs on `a535d01808057b7c921d5b50a4b0567aa7ad391a`, read 2026-11-08T18:26Z and again at 18:31Z before posting: every completed run is `success` (Build Core, Lint & Repo Gates and its seven scoped lint jobs, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · consumer gates, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Auto Label, Flag docs, Plan Test Core shards, Test Core (4/8), filter); the UI, docs, temporal-conformance and opt-in jobs are `skipped` by path filter. `Test Core (1/8, 2/8, 3/8, 5/8, 6/8, 7/8, 8/8)` and `Type Check · workspace` were still `in_progress` at the second read; their conclusions are the gate verdicts for those families and this record does not stand in for them.

### ① Derived judgments

The surface is `@objectstack/driver-sql` on the Oracle dialect only. `index.ts` re-exports nothing from `sql-driver-oracle-dialect.ts`, so the package's public surface gains only three `protected` members on `SqlDriver` (`primeOracleRawUuidColumns`, `readOracleRawUuidColumns`, `oracleUuidBinding`) and one `protected` map — additive, subclass-visible, patch-level. Every other dialect's compiled SQL and bindings are byte-identical: each priming call, `oracleUuidBinding`, the `coerceFilterValue` arm, the three refusal sites and the `formatInput` arm are gated on `isOracle`; `readBackInsertedRows` collapses to `main`'s `String(row.id)` keying exactly when the binding returns the id itself (strict equality), which is every non-Oracle call. Right, and pinned with a poisoned registry on pg, mysql2, mssql and sqlite.

The accept set on an Oracle column the catalog reports as `RAW(16)`, input class by input class (comparand under `=`, `$eq`, `$ne`, `$in`, `$nin`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$between`; a written value; a by-id key), `main` against the head:

- Dashed uuid text, either case (the form the column reads back as): `main` bound it as a VARCHAR2 and Oracle's implicit character-to-RAW conversion refuses the hyphens (ORA-01465) — the request FAILED. Head binds `HEXTORAW(?)` over the 32 upper-case digits and it works. This is the card. Widening, right.
- The 32 digits undashed, either case (the `RAWTOHEX` form): `main`'s implicit conversion accepted it, so a filter matched and a write stored the right bytes — SUCCEEDED. Head accepts it, binds the same 16 bytes, and the create read-back maps an upper-case or undashed written id to the read form. No request lost. Right.
- Even-length hex of another length (`'0f8fad5b'`): `main` converted it to a shorter RAW, so a comparand compared false and answered zero rows, and a written value landed in the `RAW(16)` column as a 4-byte value the read side cannot present as the field (`oracleRaw16AsUuid` leaves a non-16-byte RAW as a `Buffer`). Both SUCCEEDED on `main`; both are now refused before anything is sent (`INVALID_FILTER` / `VALIDATION_ERROR`, 400). This is the one input class where a request that completed on `main` now fails. It never named a row by the uuid the column reads as, and the stored case put a value in a uuid field that the field's own type cannot carry. Card item 2 orders exactly this refusal. Judged against the published spec on `main`: `type-compat.ts` holds the `oracle` / `uuid` pairing at `'lossy'` through `demoteExact`, whose JSDoc says the field "displays correctly and cannot yet be filtered or written by its value" — no declared capability covered these inputs, so the refusal makes the field type's own refusal real rather than taking a declared capability away. Not a Clause-② narrowing.
- An empty string written to such a field: Oracle stores a bound `''` as NULL, so on `main` `{ account: '' }` cleared the lookup — SUCCEEDED. Head refuses it with `VALIDATION_ERROR`; `null` still clears it (the `v === null` arm is kept). Same judgment as the class above: `''` is not an id of any row and the driver already refuses `''` as an Oracle comparand on these operators (`assertOracleComparandNotEmptyString`) prescribing `$null`. Recorded as finding 1 (nit) so the loss is on the record; it does not change the declaration.
- Non-hex text (`'not-a-uuid'`, `'acct-17'`, a nanoid), a number: ORA-01465 on `main` — FAILED. Head answers a typed 400 with the accepted forms named. Not a narrowing; a better error. Odd-length hex: NOT MEASURED on either side; it cannot name a row by the uuid the column reads as, so the same judgment holds.
- `null` as comparand or written value: `IS NULL` and a null bind, unchanged. Right.
- Pattern operators (`$contains`, `$like`, and the rest) on the same column: compiled from the text pattern exactly as on `main`, unjudged — their comparand is never bound to the column as a value. Right, and the set they are excluded by (`ORACLE_EMPTY_STRING_SENSITIVE_OPERATORS`) is exactly the set of operators whose coerced comparand reaches the column as a bind in `applyFilterCondition`'s switch, checked arm by arm.
- A `VARCHAR2` column holding uuids, a uuid-shaped value in a text column: bound as text, unchanged, because the catalog decides and the value never does. Right, pinned (the two controls).
- A failed catalog read: nothing recorded, every value binds text as on `main`, the next door asks again. An empty answer is recorded and binds text. Right; see finding 2.
- Reads: the fetch type handler and `oracleRaw16AsUuid` are untouched; a `RAW(16)` still reads as lowercase hyphenated uuid text. Right.

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and on the changeset is the right line: the only requests that stop completing on `main` are ones the published pairing never promised and the field type refuses by definition; the request the card exists for could not complete on `main` at all.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/31390-oracle-raw16-uuid-hextoraw.md`: `'@objectstack/driver-sql': patch`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial, matching the PR body's two lines. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing an author can write changes — `packages/spec` is untouched (the claim forbade a `type-compat` value change; that is #31592), no key, accepted value or default moves. A `none` kind takes `patch`, and a bug fix in a released package takes `patch`; the diff publishes from no other released package. The public-surface delta (①, protected members only) is additive. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. open_questions 1 — a comparand or written value that is not uuid text reached Oracle on `main` and is now refused: option A (keep the refusal). Answered in ①: the two input classes that completed on `main` (other-length even hex; `''` on write) never named a row by the uuid the column reads as, the pairing was published `'lossy'` with no filter/write promise, and the card orders the refusal.
2. open_questions 2 — `create()` without an id mints a nanoid, now `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400 on a `RAW(16)`-keyed object instead of an Oracle error: not a narrowing (a nanoid never converted on `main`; ORA-01465 both before and after, now typed). Option A is right and is the seat's: a database-default id (`DEFAULT SYS_GUID()`, reading the key back) is new behaviour outside the card's three items and is filed as its own card by the seat if wanted; the acceptance note already records it.
3. deviation — no second merge of `origin/main` before the PR: read live. `git log 133f75ae..origin/main -- packages/drivers/driver-sql` is empty at `origin/main` `8784ccbc`, so for every path in scope the head's tree is `main` plus this diff. #31395 has not landed (only #31381 did, before the merge base); the claim's "merge again after #31395 lands, the later lander resolves" stays owed to the seat, not to this review.
4. Live Oracle NOT MEASURED: the live cell is written (card item 4's three pins — filter eq/$in, write, lookup round-trip — plus key, control, update/delete by key and both refusals) and skips without `OS_TEST_ORACLE_URL`, which no workflow sets. What the live cell would measure rests on two things read here: Oracle's documented implicit character-to-RAW conversion and `HEXTORAW`, and the `knex.raw` row shape on `oracledb`, which `oracleRawUuidColumns` reads exactly as `rowsOf` in `sql-driver-oracle-introspection.ts` does (`Array.isArray(result)`), the reading #31328 measured on 23ai. Stays a measurement debt on the card, not a finding on the tree.
5. Forced test change — one `DOORS` row for `assertOracleUuidComparand` in `sql-driver-compile-refusal-seam.test.ts`: right; that file enumerates every builder that raises through the withheld-filter seam and is red until each has a row.
6. `textMatchPredicate` untouched, `packages/spec` untouched: right (patterns are never bound; item 3 is #31592).
7. Check-runs still `in_progress` at posting (18:31Z): `Test Core (1/8, 2/8, 3/8, 5/8, 6/8, 7/8, 8/8)` and `Type Check · workspace`. Their conclusions are read off the head by the seat before any landing act; this record does not stand in for them.

### ④ Design judgment

Contract read sentence by sentence against the tree (card items 1, 2, 4; the seat's claim's file surface).

**"A comparand or written value for a `RAW(16)` column typed as uuid binds through `HEXTORAW(?)` with dashes stripped."** `sql-driver-oracle-dialect.ts` `oracleUuidRawBinding`: `knex.raw('HEXTORAW(?)', [hex stripped, upper-cased])`; `UUID_TEXT` accepts 8-4-4-4-12 or 32 hex digits, either case. Comparands: `sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts` `coerceFilterValue` routes a uuid-text comparand on a catalogued field to the binding ahead of the temporal arm, maps arrays member by member, and stays total (a non-uuid value is returned as it is, so the `$ne` emitter's reliance on a total coercion holds). Written values: `sql-driver-sqlite-serialisation.ts` `formatInput`'s Oracle arm, keyed by logical field before `applyWriteColumnMap`, copy-on-write (the #24835 shape: the caller's `data` is never mutated, so the knex `Raw` never reaches a `DataEvent`). By-id keys: `update` binds the key once and uses it for the statement and the read-back; `delete`, `bulkDelete` (each id) and `readBackInsertedRows` (each written id, matched back by the read form) bind the same way; `bulkUpdate` delegates to `update` per item. Agrees.

**"The read side stays `RAWTOHEX` dashed."** No hunk touches the fetch type handler or `oracleRaw16AsUuid`; `oracleUuidReadForm` reproduces its exact form for the read-back match. Agrees.

**"The column type must be known at bind time; read it from the introspected/declared column type, never guess it from the value."** `sql-driver-field-mapping.ts` `primeOracleRawUuidColumns` reads `ALL_TAB_COLUMNS` (`DATA_TYPE = 'RAW' AND DATA_LENGTH = 16`) for the object's remote table, owner resolved remoteSchema, then the `OWNER.` prefix of the remote name, then `CURRENT_SCHEMA` — the same resolution the statements get (`physicalTableByObject` is the builder's table name, `physicalSchemaByObject` its schema). Columns map back to fields through `columnFieldByObject`, falling back to the column name. The value is consulted nowhere for the decision: the two controls (a `VARCHAR2` uuid column, a uuid in a text column) pin that, and ablation C4 shows them red when the value decides. The priming runs at the top of all 13 door bodies that compile a WHERE or a write for an object (find/findOne through `findRows`, create, update, delete, bulkCreate, bulkDelete, updateMany, deleteMany, count, aggregate, distinct, findWithWindowFunctions, analyzeQuery — `explain` goes through `analyzeQuery`; `upsert` is refused by name on Oracle before any statement, so the upsert-family `where(idColumn, …)` sites it alone reaches are rightly untouched). Agrees for every door's own object; see finding 3 for the one filter that compiles a second object's predicate.

**"Malformed uuid text is refused with a typed `INVALID_FILTER`, not sent."** `assertOracleUuidComparand` at the three sites that bind a comparison comparand (`compileFilters` bare `=`; `applyFilterCondition` operator path, inside the existing `if (this.isOracle)` block; `applyFilterCondition` bare `=`), through `withheldFilterError` with the refusing subtree, so the field is withheld unless author-marked — the same seam the empty-string refusal uses; a by-key door's id has no subtree and is withheld. `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 reused, no new code. Written values take `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400, the family `sql-driver-top-level.ts` already refuses an unwritable value with. Nothing is sent before either: the find-door and create-door tests assert an empty statement log, and in `create` the refusal is raised by `formatInput` ahead of the INSERT (the autonumber reservation that precedes it does not apply to a federated object). Agrees.

**"Catalog read once per object; failure modes."** `has(object)` short-circuits; a non-federated object has no `physicalTableByObject` entry (its only writer is `registerExternalObject`) and returns without a read; a thrown read records nothing and the next door asks again (pinned); an empty answer is recorded (pinned); `registerExternalObject` deletes the recording so a re-pointed object is read again (pinned). Concurrency: two first doors on one object in flight together both read and both set the same value — benign; see finding 4 for the in-flight re-registration edge. Agrees.

**Other dialects byte-identical.** Judged in ①; the four pins run with the registry deliberately poisoned so only the dialect guard keeps the arm out, and they pass on `main`'s source too. Agrees.

**Facade.** `sql-driver.ts` adds one-line forwards and host installs only; the catalog read is split into `readOracleRawUuidColumns` so a test can stub it without a connection — right, and `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries the facade and keyed-text gates) is green on the head.

**Tests.** `sql-driver-oracle-dialect.test.ts`: 30 tests over a probe that answers the catalog from a fixture and captures `_query` — compile pins for every comparison shape the card names, the two controls, five refusal shapes plus the door, insert/null/update/delete/bulkDelete/read-back SQL, the four catalog pins, the four other-dialect pins. `sql-driver-oracle-federation-conformance.test.ts`: the live cell (③.4). Both do what they claim; the negative pins were ablated one by one in the report.

Findings, graded:

1. **nit** — `formatInput` Oracle arm (`sql-driver-sqlite-serialisation.ts`): an empty string written to a catalogued `RAW(16)` field is `VALIDATION_ERROR` where `main` stored NULL. Keep: `null` is the spelling that means no value and is kept, and the comparand side already refuses `''` prescribing `$null`. On the record for ①.
2. **nit** — `primeOracleRawUuidColumns` swallows a failed catalog read with no log line. The next statement then fails visibly at Oracle (ORA-01465 on the text bind), so this is a functional degradation and `warn` is its level under AGENTS.md's rule; a one-time `warn` naming the object and that uuid binding fell back to text would let an operator connect the two. Same shape as `primeMssqlPagingKey`.
3. **nit** — `readableIdsSubquery` (`sql-driver-internal-helpers.ts`, read) applies a permission scope's filter on a *parent* object's builder without priming that object; if the parent is an Oracle federated object no door has touched in this driver, a `RAW(16)` comparand in the scope binds text — `main`'s behaviour, never worse — until the parent's first door primes it. The function is synchronous, so the fix belongs to the doors (prime the objects named by composed-readable-ids leaves in `where`). Narrow enough to note; the seat files it if wanted.
4. **nit** — `primeOracleRawUuidColumns` is check-then-await-then-set: a `registerExternalObject` for the same object during the in-flight read is overwritten by the now-stale set when the read resolves. Same shape as `primeMssqlPagingKey`; a re-check of `has` after the await, or keying the recording by remote table, closes it.
5. **nit** — the predicate `this.oracleRawUuidFieldsByObject.get(table ?? '')?.has(field) === true` is spelled at four sites in `sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts`; one named helper would make the three refusal sites and the coercion arm read as one rule.
6. **nit** — no Oracle compile pin for `$between` or the ordered comparisons over a `RAW(16)` column; knex's `parameter()` unwraps a `Raw` for `whereBetween` and `where(col, op, raw)` by the same path `whereIn` uses, which is pinned, so correctness is not in doubt.
7. **nit** — a remote name that is a synonym is absent from `ALL_TAB_COLUMNS`, so the answer is empty, cached, and the field binds text as on `main` (a view is listed and works). Worth a sentence in `oracleRawUuidColumns`'s docblock.

No must-fix, no should-fix. Nits alone end the round.
